common_name: Daily Double Daylily (Vintage Orange Double Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained garden soil in full sun; Daily Double is a mid-1940s heirloom diploid whose orange self flowers usually open with extra petaloids in the center, though some flowers on a scape may revert to single form from day to day.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained garden soil in full sun; Daily Double is one of the earliest named double-flowered daylily cultivars, dating to the mid-1940s, bearing orange self blooms with three extra petaloids and stamens clustered in the center of most flowers, giving a fuller, rounder look than typical single daylily form. Not every flower on a scape doubles fully, some open single the following day, a quirk typical of early double-flower breeding before the trait was stabilized in later cultivars. This semi-evergreen diploid blooms in midseason on clumps that increase steadily. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous bloom.

common_name: Early Early Truffle Daylily (Early-Blooming Cream Double Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Early Early Truffle opens its creamy blush double blooms notably earlier in the season than most daylily cultivars, giving a head start on the daylily bloom season.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Early Early Truffle bears creamy blush double flowers that consistently hold their full, ruffled double form, opening notably earlier in the season than most daylily cultivars and giving gardeners a jump start on the daylily display before mainstream midseason types begin flowering. The clump builds into a full, floriferous stand over a few seasons. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy early bloom.

common_name: Forever Young Daylily (Fragrant Double Yellow Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Forever Young, registered in the mid-1970s, carries bright yellow double flowers in heavy midsummer flush for several weeks.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Forever Young bears medium-sized, fragrant, bright yellow double flowers that open in such profusion that the clump appears topped with distinctive yellow balls through several weeks of midsummer bloom. This older, garden-tough double daylily increases readily into a full stand. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain heavy flowering.

common_name: Venetian Fringe Daylily (Rose Double Daylily with Gold Fringe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Venetian Fringe is a modern tetraploid double daylily, registered in 2008, that reliably doubles on nearly every bloom.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Venetian Fringe bears large rose-colored double flowers over seven inches across, each petal and petaloid trimmed in a gold, sawtooth-fringed edge above a green throat. This semi-evergreen tetraploid carries a high bud count per scape and dependably opens in double form roughly nineteen times out of twenty, blooming through midseason with some rebloom. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Double Pardon Me Daylily (Fragrant Double Red Miniature Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Double Pardon Me is a double-flowered sport of the popular compact reblooming daylily 'Pardon Me,' sharing its parent's deep cranberry-red color and compact habit but with many extra tepals.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Double Pardon Me bears brilliant cranberry-red double flowers that can carry as many as eighteen tepals instead of the usual six, giving each bloom a lush, full-petaled look while keeping the compact, floriferous habit of its parent cultivar 'Pardon Me.' This fragrant diploid reblooms steadily from early to midsummer and again later in the season, attracting bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain heavy flowering.

common_name: Little Wild Flower Daylily (Coral Red Miniature Double Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Little Wild Flower, registered in 1997, is a true miniature double daylily with compact 13-inch scapes well suited to pots and small-garden edging.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; Little Wild Flower is a true miniature double daylily bearing coral-red blend flowers only about two inches across above a green throat, opening in profusion on compact scapes around 13 inches tall. This diploid reblooms over an early-to-midseason display and its small, tidy scale suits containers, rock gardens, and the front edge of a border where larger daylilies would overwhelm the space. Divide every few years in spring as clumps thicken to maintain heavy bud count.

common_name: Little Suzie Daylily (Gold Miniature Daylily with Red Eyezone)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Little Suzie, registered in 1971, is a classic true miniature daylily with scapes only about a foot tall.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Little Suzie is a classic true miniature daylily bearing light gold flowers only about two inches wide, marked with a small rose-red eyezone and a matching red throat, held on scapes just around a foot tall. This evergreen cultivar blooms in midseason with an extended flowering period and multiplies into a dense, grassy clump. Its diminutive scale makes it useful for edging, rock gardens, and small-space plantings. Divide every few years in spring to sustain heavy bud count.

common_name: Sweet Seneca Petite Daylily (Pink Miniature Daylily with Raspberry Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Sweet Seneca Petite, registered in 2008, is a true miniature daylily with scapes only about 10 inches tall, among the smallest-statured cultivars grown.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; Sweet Seneca Petite is a diminutive true miniature daylily bearing light pink flowers about two inches across, marked by a dark raspberry eyezone above a yellow-to-green throat, held on scapes only around 10 inches tall. This dormant diploid blooms in midseason and propagates only by division since it will not come true from seed. Its very compact scale makes it an excellent choice for rock gardens, troughs, and the front edge of a bed. Divide every few years in spring as clumps fill in.

common_name: Just My Size Daylily (Pink and Mauve Miniature Double Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Just My Size, registered in 2000, is an exceptionally compact miniature double daylily standing only about 6 to 12 inches tall.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Just My Size is an exceptionally compact miniature double daylily, standing just 6 to 12 inches tall, with small pink and rose-mauve double flowers produced in abundance from early midseason into a reliable rebloom. Its sturdy, prolific habit and tiny stature make it ideal for containers, rock gardens, and the very front edge of a mixed border where full-size daylilies would be out of scale. Divide every few years in spring to keep clumps full and floriferous.

common_name: Judy Judy Daylily (Strongly Fragrant Lavender Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Judy Judy, registered in 1998, is valued among fragrant daylily cultivars for its strongly perfumed, six-inch lavender blooms.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Judy Judy bears bold, strongly fragrant lavender flowers about six inches across, with a golden-yellow throat and petals edged in a tight, ruffled gold picotee. This tetraploid, semi-evergreen cultivar blooms from mid to late summer and its noticeably strong perfume, unusual in modern large-flowered hybrids, makes it a good choice sited near a patio, walkway, or open window where the scent can be appreciated. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Frosted Vintage Ruffles Daylily (Very Fragrant Cream and Pink Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Frosted Vintage Ruffles, registered in 2000, is classed as very fragrant, among the more strongly scented modern daylily introductions.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Frosted Vintage Ruffles bears large, very fragrant flowers about 4.5 inches across in a soft cream blend with a darker pink, heavily ruffled edge above a yellow-green throat. This diploid blooms early in the season and reblooms, carrying around twenty buds across four branches per scape for a long display. Its strong, pleasant fragrance is noticeable from several feet away on warm mornings, making it a good candidate for borders near seating areas. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.
